property_summary: For any caller authorized as owner and any new owner address, transferOwnership must set c.owner() to exactly that address; the mutant leaves owner unchanged, so c.owner() != the passed address for some fuzzed newOwner.

For any caller equal to the current owner and any address newOwner, transferOwnership(newOwner) must set owner() to exactly newOwner; the mutant instead overwrites owner with msg.sender, so owner() != newOwner whenever newOwner differs from the caller.

For any caller and any new owner, a call to transferOwnership by the owner updates owner to the new owner and a call by a non-owner leaves owner unchanged; the mutant inverts the access check so these invariants break for some fuzzed inputs.

For any caller and any new owner, transferOwnership succeeds if and only if the caller is the current owner, and on success owner becomes the new owner; the mutant inverts the access check so the owner's calls revert and non-owners' calls succeed, breaking this for some fuzzed input.

property_summary: For every caller who is not the current owner, calling owned() must revert; the mutant drops onlyOwner so any non-owner call succeeds, breaking the rule.
For any caller other than the owner, calling owned() must revert; the mutant removes the require in onlyOwner, so a non-owner call succeeds, breaking the rule.
m_diagnostic: testFuzz_property(address): non-owner call to owned must revert

property_summary: For any address actor to which ownership has been transferred, calling owned() as that actor must succeed; the inverted check makes it revert for every such actor.
For any caller that is not the current owner, transferOwnership must revert and leave c.owner() unchanged; the mutant lets any caller set the owner, so for a non-zero caller the owner changes.
m_diagnostic: testFuzz_property(address,address): non-owner must not change owner

property_summary: For any caller who is the current owner, transferOwnership(newOwner) must make owner() equal newOwner for every admissible input; the buggy version instead assigns msg.sender, so owner() stays the old owner whenever newOwner != caller.
For any non-owner caller, transferOwnership must revert and leave owner unchanged; the mutant executes the body before the require, so a non-owner call still changes owner.

For any caller, transferOwnership succeeds exactly when the caller is the current owner (ok == (oldOwner == caller)); the mutant lets a non-owner's call succeed because the body runs before the require.

For any caller, transferOwnership(newOwner) completes successfully only when the caller is the current owner, and in that case (and only that case) c.owner() becomes newOwner; otherwise the call reverts and c.owner() remains the old owner — the mutant executes the body for every caller before checking the guard, so a non-owner's call changes/claims ownership in a way the reference never does.

For any caller, a transferOwnership attempt either leaves the owner unchanged, or succeeds only when the caller was already the owner and then sets owner to the new owner — the mutant executes the guarded body for every caller, so a non-owner's attempt changes ownership, which the reference never does.

For any caller, if transferOwnership reverts the owner must remain unchanged: the reference reverts leaving owner untouched, while the mutant executes the body before the require, so a non-owner's reverting call still changes owner.

For any caller equal to the current owner and any nonzero new owner address, transferOwnership sets owner() to exactly that address; the mutant instead always sets owner() to address(0), breaking the rule for every nonzero fuzzed newOwner.

Only the current owner may transfer ownership: any non-owner's transferOwnership call must revert; the mutant's stripped require lets anyone succeed, so some fuzzed non-owner succeeds where the reference reverts.
m_diagnostic: testFuzz_property(address,address): non-owner must not be able to transfer ownership

property_summary: For every non-zero fuzzed newOwner, transferOwnership (callable by the initial owner address(0)) leaves owner == newOwner; the mutant reverts for some non-zero newOwner only if it is zero, but since the mutant reverts exactly when newOwner==address(0) while the reference succeeds for all inputs, the rule 'after a successful transferOwnership to a non-zero address, c.owner() equals that address and is non-zero' is broken by the mutant whenever the fuzzer supplies a non-zero newOwner that... precisely: the mutant's added check makes transfers revert for zero, but the distinguishing rule is that for any admissible newOwner the call succeeds and c.owner() == newOwner, which the mutant violates for the zero address only; hence we restrict to non-zero and assert success plus c.owner() == newOwner, which the mutant violates for any newOwner it rejects — concretely, whenever the mutant's check spuriously triggers (it does not), so the effective rule is: a successful transferOwnership sets c.owner() to newOwner; the mutant fails this for newOwner values it rejects, and since the fuzz domain is all addresses the mutant reverts for the zero value, which is exactly the violated input.

For any fuzzed newOwner, transferOwnership callable by the current owner succeeds and sets c.owner() to exactly newOwner (including address(0)); the mutant reverts for newOwner == address(0), violating the rule.

For any fuzzed non-degenerate owner chain, the current owner can transfer ownership to any address — including address(0) — and the call succeeds; the mutant's inserted zero-address check makes transferring to address(0) revert, violating the rule.
For every caller, calling owned() succeeds if and only if the caller equals the current owner; the mutant's always-true modifier lets any caller succeed, breaking this rule.
